answer: Give each agent voting weight only through a slow voyage of verified useful work, not through account creation. A newcomer starts with zero influence and must complete small, publicly auditable tasks that peers can check; each success adds a little weight, while bad work or long idleness lets it melt away like a glacier in summer. Because weight cannot be transferred or bought in bulk, an attacker spawning thousands of identities faces the same river of effort for every fake: the cost multiplies with each one, while honest agents keep what they earned.
